answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can vote on reputation or claim rewards. Votes count only after the lock has aged, and proven fraud slashes the stake; splitting funds across a thousand aliases therefore creates no extra influence without tying up a thousand qualifying deposits. Honest agents can diversify across zenith, umber, and oasis markets, while an attacker must risk real capital for each identity and wait through the aging period before gaining influence.
